proposed_definition_changes.reason: A one-quarter sphere net has cardinality at most \(9^{J_n}\), so the union-bound entropy is order \(J_n\), not \(J_n\log(1+J_n)\). The conditional vector second-moment calculation likewise gives the cross-moment rate of order \(\sqrt{J_n/n_{C,\min}}\). The corrected gauges propagate these sharper rates through \(\zeta_{G,n}\), \(\zeta_{c,n}\), \(\eta_{\Pi,n}\), and \(\Gamma_n\) without altering their algebraic definitions.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each evaluation fold, bridge dictionaries are learned on a construction subsample, projection coefficients are fitted on a disjoint calibration subsample with an empirical spectral cutoff and ridge, and the resulting affine signal is evaluated only on the held-out fold. Fourth-moment multiplier envelopes yield the exact dimension-aware dictionary error \(\delta_{D,n}\). A conditional Bernstein inequality over a \(1/4\)-net and a direct conditional second-moment calculation give the sharpened calibration gauges \(\eta_{G,n}=B_{D,n}^2\{\sqrt{J_n/n_{C,\min}}+J_n/n_{C,\min}\}\) and \(\eta_{c,n}=B_{D,n}B_{0,n}\sqrt{J_n/n_{C,\min}}\). Thus, for bounded calibration envelopes, the calibration consistency requirement is \(J_n/n_{C,\min}\to0\). Population positive-eigenvalue separation, the spectral cutoff, ridge and coefficient-envelope conditions, and \(\Gamma_n=o_p(1)\) then imply learned efficient-signal convergence; a root-\(n\) primal-dual product condition gives the one-step expansion.

statement_notes.justification: Conditional on the construction sample, a sphere-net Bernstein argument with \(|\mathcal N_{J_n}|\le9^{J_n}\) controls the learned Gram operator at the log-free dimension rate, while a direct conditional second-moment calculation controls the score--dictionary vector; a finite fold union bound supplies the asserted uniformity.
statement_notes.gap: No proof gap remains under the declared conditional moment-generating-function envelope and fixed-fold condition. With bounded envelopes, the resulting calibration gauges vanish when \(J_n/n_{C,\min}\to0\), without a \(\log(1+J_n)\) loss.
statement_notes.consumer: The sharpened bounds propagate through \(\zeta_{G,n}\), \(\zeta_{c,n}\), \(\eta_{\Pi,n}\), and \(\Gamma_n\), and feed the singular-Gram projector and resolvent perturbation in \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\).
